repairs.before: When Jin reached Chenggao, Yao Guang in Luoyang begged for reinforcements.
repairs.after: When the Jin army reached Chenggao, Yao Guang, General Who Conquers the South, was garrisoning Luoyang. He sent a rider at speed to request relief.
repairs.sourceWitness: 王師至成皋，征南姚洸時鎮洛陽，馳使請救。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Guang’s military title, the Luoyang garrison and his urgent mounted messenger.

repairs.before: Yao Hong sent Yan Sheng with three thousand horse, Yao Yinan with ten thousand foot to Luoyang, and Yao Yi to Shan ford as a screen.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yan Sheng, colonel of the Yue Cavalry, with three thousand horsemen to the rescue and the Martial Guard commander Yao Yinan with ten thousand infantry to help defend Luoyang. He also sent Yao Yi, General Who Conquers the East and governor of Bingzhou, south to camp at Shan Ford in support.
repairs.sourceWitness: 泓遣越騎校尉閻生率騎三千以赴之，武衛姚益男將步卒一萬助守洛陽，又遣征東、并州牧姚懿南屯陝津為之聲援。
repairs.sourceReason: The officers have distinct titles, Yi was ordered south to camp at Shan Ford, and his force was to support the relief effort.

repairs.after: Guang’s subordinate commander Zhao Xuan urged him, “The invaders have already penetrated deep into our territory. The people are terrified, and our forces are so outnumbered that it will be hard to meet the enemy.

repairs.sourceReason: Restore Xuan’s relationship to Guang, the depth of the incursion and the difficulty of meeting the enemy.

repairs.before: Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang, and Wulao fell; Tan Daoji rolled forward unchecked.
repairs.after: Meanwhile Yangcheng, Chenggao, Xingyang and Wulao all surrendered, and Tan Daoji and the others advanced swiftly without a check.

repairs.sourceReason: 悉降 means all four cities surrendered; restore Daoji’s companions.

repairs.before: Zhao Xuan fought Mao Dezu at Baigu, was overrun and cut down; Qian Jian tried to drag him clear but Zhao said, "I am finished—save yourself."
repairs.after: At Baigu, Zhao Xuan fought the Jin general Mao Dezu and was defeated by superior numbers. He received more than ten wounds and cried out from the ground. His major, Qian Jian, braved the blades to hold him in his arms and wept. Xuan said, “My wounds are grave. You must leave at once.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 玄與晉將毛德祖戰于柏穀，以眾寡而敗，被瘡十餘，據地大呼，玄司馬騫鑒冒刃抱玄而泣，玄曰：「吾瘡已重，君宜速去。」
repairs.sourceReason: The English omits numerical inferiority, more than ten wounds, the cry and Jian’s tears, and inserts an attempt to drag Xuan away.

repairs.before: Qian Jian said, "If you fall, I fall with you."
repairs.after: Qian Jian replied, “If you do not survive, General, I will die with you. If I left, where would I go?”
repairs.sourceWitness: 鑒曰：「若將軍不濟，當與俱死，去將安之！」
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Jian’s rhetorical refusal to leave.

repairs.before: Yan Sheng and Yao Yinan stopped cold when they heard Luoyang was lost.
repairs.after: Yan Sheng had reached Xin’an and Yao Yinan had reached Hucheng. Luoyang had already fallen, so they stayed in camp and advanced no farther.
repairs.sourceWitness: 時閻生至新安，益男至湖城，會洛陽已沒，遂留屯不進。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore each officer’s location and the decision to remain in camp without advancing.

repairs.before: Prince Yao Yi was vain and credulous; Sun Chang urged him to strike Chang'an, kill Yao Shao, and seize the throne.
repairs.after: Yao Yi was mean and treacherous and easily misled by those he trusted. His major Sun Chang, a cunning flatterer who delighted in turmoil and misfortune, urged him to raid Chang’an, kill Yao Shao, depose Yao Hong and set himself on the throne.
repairs.sourceWitness: 姚懿嶮薄，惑於信受，其司馬孫暢奸巧傾佞，好亂樂禍，勸懿襲長安，誅姚紹，廢泓自立。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Yi’s mean and treacherous disposition, Sun Chang’s staff office and delight in trouble, and the explicit deposition of Hong.

repairs.before: Yao Yi marched to Shan ford and scattered state grain to buy tribal loyalty.
repairs.after: Yi took his advice and led troops to Shan Ford. He distributed grain to the non-Chinese and Chinese inhabitants north of the Yellow River, intending to deplete the state reserves, attract the Qiang groups of Herong and win personal credit for the largesse.

repairs.sourceReason: 河北 is north of the Yellow River. Yi distributes to both indigenous and Chinese people and seeks separately to drain state reserves, draw in the Herong Qiang and cultivate personal favor.

repairs.sourceReason: Restore Hong’s hearing the report, the other summoned advisers and the court hall.

repairs.before: Yao Shao said: "Yao Yi is weak-minded; Sun Chang made him do this.
repairs.after: Yao Shao said, “Yi is narrow in outlook and easily swayed by others. Sun Chang must be the one behind this affair.
repairs.sourceWitness: 紹曰：「懿性識鄙近，從物推移，造成此事，惟當孫暢耳。
repairs.sourceReason: Shao explains Yi’s limited judgment and susceptibility to influence; Sun Chang’s authorship is an inference.

repairs.before: Arrest Sun Chang, put Yao Zan in Shan, and I will take Tong Pass—if they obey, Yao Yi can still march east against Jin.
repairs.after: Just send a swift rider to summon Sun Chang, and send Pacifying General Yao Zan to hold the city of Shan. I will go to Tong Pass to direct the armies. If Chang comes in obedience to the edict, I will have Yi lead the troops now available in Hedong to join us against the invaders from Wu.
repairs.sourceWitness: 但馳使征暢，遣撫軍贊據陝城，臣向潼關為諸軍節度，若暢奉詔而至者，臣當遣懿率河東見兵共平吳寇。
repairs.sourceReason: 征暢 summons Chang; it does not order his arrest. He is to comply with the edict, and Yi would lead the existing troops of Hedong alongside Shao against the southern invaders.

repairs.before: Only dispatch riders at speed to summon Chang; send General Who Pacifies Zan to hold Shan city; I will go to Tong Pass to command all armies—if Chang comes bearing the edict, I will order Yi to lead Hedong's available troops together to pacify the Wu bandit.

repairs.before: If they defy the edict, publish their treason and attack."
repairs.after: If rebellion is already under way and they resist the edict, we should proclaim their crime to the realm and sound the drums to attack them.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 如其逆釁已成，違距詔敕者，當明其罪於天下，聲鼓以擊之。」
repairs.sourceReason: Shao makes the plan conditional on an established breach and resistance to the edict, and directs sounding the attack drums.

repairs.before: He sent Yao Zan, Simo Guofan, and She Xuan to Shan and Yao Lü to Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.
repairs.sourceWitness: 於是遣姚贊及冠軍司馬國璠、建義蛇玄屯陝津，武衛姚驢屯潼關。
repairs.sourceReason: 司馬 is the surname Sima; 冠軍 is the rank. Weishu 37 explicitly names 冠軍將軍司馬國璠. Restore both stations and commanders’ titles. https://www.shidianguji.com/zh/book/LS0010/chapter/LS0010_152

repairs.before: Thereupon he sent Yao Zan and champion major Simo Guofan, Jianyi She Xuan to camp at Shan ford, Martial Guard Yao Lü to camp at Tong Pass.
repairs.after: Hong sent Yao Zan, Champion General Sima Guofan and General She Xuan, holder of the title Jianyi, to encamp at Shan Ford, and Martial Guard commander Yao Lü to encamp at Tong Pass.

repairs.before: Yao Yi declared himself ruler and tried to ship grain from Xiongnu Fort to his troops.
repairs.after: Yao Yi raised troops, claimed the sovereign title and circulated proclamations to the provinces and commanderies. He sought to move grain from the Xiongnu fort to provision the garrison.
repairs.sourceWitness: 懿遂舉兵僭號，傳檄州郡，欲運匈奴堡穀以給鎮人。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore the raising of troops and proclamations to provinces and commanderies.

repairs.before: Yao Chengdu blocked him; Yao Yi tried flattery and sent a pledge knife—Chengdu handed it to Yao Hong.
repairs.after: Yao Chengdu, General Who Pacifies the East, resisted him. Yi tried to win Chengdu over with humble words and bind him closely to himself, sending his belt knife as a pledge. Chengdu sent the knife on to Hong.
repairs.sourceWitness: 甯東姚成都距之，懿乃卑辭招誘，深自結托，送佩刀為誓，成都送以呈泓。
repairs.sourceReason: Restore Chengdu’s title and Yi’s attempt to bind him personally with a knife from his belt.

repairs.before: Chengdu captured Wang Guo and scolded Yao Yi: "As the emperor's uncle you should steady the throne, not plot treason.
repairs.after: Yi then sent the Valiant Cavalry commander Wang Guo with several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu. Chengdu captured and imprisoned Guo and sent Yi this rebuke: “As the emperor’s younger brother by the same mother, you were entrusted with military command. The state now hangs as precariously as a dangling tassel. You ought to serve with reverent care and diligence and uphold the royal house.
repairs.sourceWitness: 懿又遣驍騎王國率甲士數百攻成都，成都擒國，囚之，遣讓懿曰：「明公以母弟之親，受推轂之寄，今社稷之危若綴旒然，宜恭恪憂勤，匡輔王室。
repairs.sourceReason: The speaker is Chengdu, the target is Yi, the emperor’s younger full brother (as at s0120). 推轂 signifies the trust of military command. Restore Guo’s office, several hundred armored men, capture and imprisonment, and the dangling-tassel image of peril.

repairs.before: Yi also sent swift cavalry Wang Guo leading several hundred armored soldiers to attack Chengdu; Chengdu seized Guo, imprisoned him, sent reproach to Yi, saying, "The enlightened lord, with mother's-brother closeness, received the charge of the pushing-bar wheel; now the altars' peril hangs like a tassel—he ought reverently to toil in worry and assist the royal house.

repairs.before: The imperial ancestors will not bless a traitor.
repairs.after: Instead you harbor treachery and plot to endanger the dynasty. How could the spirits of our three ancestors rest easy over your conduct?
repairs.sourceWitness: 而更包藏奸宄，謀危宗廟，三祖之靈豈安公乎！
repairs.sourceReason: The speaker charges Yi personally with concealing treachery and scheming against his dynasty; he invokes three ancestors.

repairs.before: This grain feeds the frontier—what right have you to give it away?
repairs.after: This garrison’s grain is the support of the whole region. What merit have your garrison men shown that you would give it to them?
repairs.sourceWitness: 此鎮之糧，一方所寄，鎮人何功，而欲給之！
repairs.sourceReason: The whole region depends on this garrison’s grain; Chengdu asks what merit the proposed recipients have earned.

repairs.before: Wang Guo was a fool's errand; he waits in chains for the axe.
repairs.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
repairs.sourceWitness: 王國為蛇畫足，國之罪人，已就囚執，聽詔而戮之。
repairs.sourceReason: Guo is the state criminal and the one compared to a man gratuitously adding feet to a snake. Chengdu must await an edict before execution.

repairs.before: Wang Guo was a snake painting feet—a criminal of the state; he is already imprisoned awaiting the edict to execute him.
repairs.after: Wang Guo added feet to a snake. He is a criminal against the state and is already in custody. I await the imperial order to put him to death.
repairs.sourceWitness: 王國為蛇畫足，國之罪人，已就囚執，聽詔而戮之。
repairs.sourceReason: Guo is the state criminal and the one compared to a man gratuitously adding feet to a snake. Chengdu must await an edict before execution.

repairs.before: I am raising loyal troops to meet you on the Yellow River."
repairs.after: I am now rallying loyal men to punish your crime. When the whole army has assembled, I will meet you on the Yellow River.”
repairs.sourceWitness: 成都方糾合義眾，以懲明公之罪，復須大兵悉集，當與明公會於河上。」
repairs.sourceReason: Restore the object of punishing Yi and the condition that all the forces have assembled.

repairs.before: He called the garrisons to arms and gathered supplies.
repairs.after: Chengdu sent proclamations to the cities, exhorting them to loyalty and righteousness. He sharpened weapons, fed the horses and levied contributions for the cause.
repairs.sourceWitness: 乃宣告諸城，勉以忠義，厲兵秣馬，徵發義租。
repairs.sourceReason: Chengdu addresses the cities, exhorts them to loyal action, prepares weapons and horses, and levies contributions to the cause.

repairs.before: Thereupon he proclaimed to the cities, urged them with loyalty and righteousness, sharpened weapons and fed horses, and levied righteous rent.
